subject: general
question: Which incident intensified British control over India’s foreign trade?

options.text: British' s monopoly on foreign trade

solution:
The correct answer is __**Opening of Suez Canal**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The opening of the Suez Cana**l in 1869 greatly impacted British control over India's foreign trade.
 
• The canal provided a shorter and more efficient route for trade** between Europe and India, reducing travel time and costs.**
 
• This increased trade with Europe and gave Britain more control over India's economy and resources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The opening of the Suez Canal**__ greatly reduced the travel time and **costs for ships travelling between Europe and India.**
 
• This allowed** British merchants to trade more efficiently with India** and other parts of Asia.
 
• As a result, British businesses and** trade with India increased significantly**, which led to an **increase in British control over India's foreign trade.**
 
• **The British East India Company was the main beneficiary of this trade expansion**, as it had a** monopoly over India's foreign trade.**
 
• **The opening of the canal also led to an increase in demand for Indian goods such as cotton, tea, and spices in Europe**.
